By: Senator Barry DeKay This week, I wanted to invite in- terested Nebraska college students to consider applying for the Legis- lature’s Page Program. Legislative pages are selected in the fall each year by the Clerk of the Legislature’s Office to work in the upcoming legislative session be- ginning the following January. The Page Program maintains a nonpar- tisan role, meaning pages are se- lected regardless of political party registration. Pages respond to Senators’ re- quest lights on the floor. Pages also run errands, deliver messages, pho- tocopy materials, get food and drink for the Senators, assist the presiding officer (usually the Lieu- tenant Governor or the Speaker of the Legislature), set up and staff committee hearings, and perform other duties as assigned. An applicant for the Page Pro- gram must be a high school gradu- ate who is currently enrolled in a Nebraska college,

A combination firearm and bowhunter education course will be offered by Nebraska Game and Parks Commission volunteer instructors in Orchard on Sep- tember 21st, 24th, and 26th. The times will be 5:30pm to 9:00pm on September 21st and 24th, and 8:30am to 4:30pm on September 26th. This free course will be held at the Orchard Community Center (formerly Orchard Public School) at 407 E. 4th St. in Orchard. The course will provide instruction in safe firearms use, safe bow use, tree stand safety, shooting and sighting techniques, hunter ethics, game identification, track- ing, and conservation manage- ment. Students must attend all three sessions to complete the course. In Nebraska, hunters ages 12 through 29 must have on their person proof of successful com- pletion of firearm hunter educa- tion when hunting with a firearm.
